clue.text: Indexed material for art exhibition…

parts.note: read 'indexed' as applied with the index digit: colour put on a picture by hand rather than brush, as seen at a children's show

explanation.surface: A catalogue of items prepared for a gallery show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indexed' looks like 'listed in an index'; here it means worked with the index digit. The ellipsis runs on to the next across clue but adds nothing to the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour smeared on with the hand, a technique children use, is exactly the stuff an index digit spreads for a picture.

clue.text: Divine appropriate to English diocese

parts.note: for can mean suited or appropriate to, as in 'a job for him'
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A clergyman suited to an English bishopric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like a noun for a clergyman, fitting the diocese, but it is the verb meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to predict or perceive in advance what is to come.

clue.text: Glamorgan town rebuilt from the ruins of Athens? Not quite!

indicators.note: a building rebuilt from ruins is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
not quite the whole word: its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A Welsh town reconstructed from the remains of Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims ATHENS to ATHEN; 'rebuilt' rearranges those five letters. Glamorgan is a county in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This industrial settlement sits in the old county of Glamorgan in South Wales.

clue.text: Article in which I lead, or it is altered

indicators.note: the letters given are changed in order, signalling that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece whose writer leads, unless it is rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is altered' rearranges the nine letters of I LEAD OR IT; 'in which' is joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article expressing the paper's own opinion goes by this name.

clue.text: This head, with accent, could be 16

explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the answer to 16-down, a first course of an Italian meal; the accented word names a savoury spread often eaten as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of the skull is an old word for the head; with a circumflex it becomes a meat paste often served as a starter.

clue.text: Where striker stands-and what he is out for

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman (here 'striker') stands in the crease, the line marked at the wicket; an industrial striker is out on strike for a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside the batting line is where a batsman stands, and a pay rise is what a striking worker demands.

clue.text: Refuse lago's purse

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Othello, Iago says 'Who steals my purse steals trash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish or garbage is one sense; in Othello the villain calls his purse worthless rubbish compared with a good name.

clue.text: Freud as yearly record-keeper, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: an annalist keeps annals, records written year by year

explanation.surface: Picturing the psychoanalyst as a keeper of annual records.
explanation.walkthrough: Sigmund Freud, father of psychoanalysis, defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud founded psychoanalysis, so he is a classic example of a psychotherapist who examines minds.

clue.text: For space between electrodes, set offblank

parts.note: to spark is to set off or trigger something
a gap is a blank space

explanation.surface: Instructions for the space between electrodes: leave it empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word introducing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The air space across which an electric discharge jumps between two terminals has this technical name.

clue.text: … articles I ordered to be true to life

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Items set out in sequence so that a display looks lifelike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges the nine letters of ARTICLES and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifelike or faithful to reality is the sense of the word describing accurate portrayal.

clue.text: Star mark in examination

explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in a constellation bears the first Greek letter's name, and that same letter is a top grade given for school work.

clue.text: Followers of harrow, say

parts.note: the famous English public institution Harrow is followed by a word naming the place of learning; its pupils follow it too

explanation.surface: Gulls trailing behind a farmer's harrow across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: A harrow is a farm implement that birds follow; capitalised, Harrow is a famous English fee-paying boys' establishment, whose name is always followed by the word for a place of education.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are the body following an educational establishment, and the word naming such a place follows 'Harrow'.

clue.text: Sluggishness greatly affected by intake of hydrogen

indicators.note: the following element is taken in, so its letter goes inside the scrambled word
something affected is altered, signalling that the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Lethargy made much worse by breathing in a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges GREATLY into LETARGY; 'by intake of' puts H inside, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor or lack of energy is what sluggishness describes.

clue.text: Cake that goes like lightning in France…

explanation.surface: A pastry that vanishes quickly when served in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for lightning is also the name of a long cream-filled choux pastry; 'that goes like' is joining words, playing on how quickly such cakes are eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry finger with cream and chocolate icing carries the French word for a lightning flash.

clue.text: Abundance of ropes for making things fast

explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for plenty is one sense; cords or ties used to secure cargo are the other.

clue.text: … whereas this delicacy of theirs went slowly

definitions.text: whereas this delicacy of theirs went slowly

parts.words: whereas this delicacy of theirs went slowly
parts.note: follows the previous clue: the French have a quick pastry, but also a slow-moving dish, the garden snail served with garlic butter

explanation.surface: Contrasting a fast French pastry with a sluggish French dish.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue continues the previous one across the ellipsis: 'theirs' means the French, and the slow delicacy is a snail, the creature famous for its pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked in garlic butter are a French delicacy, and snails are proverbially slow movers.

clue.text: Not at Pisa, perhaps, this course? On the contrary!

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the words are one possible arrangement of the letters
says the relation runs the other way: the course is the rearrangement of the phrase, not the reverse

explanation.surface: A dish one is told is not served in Pisa, which the setter then contradicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' with 'On the contrary' says the answer is a rearrangement of NOT AT PISA; the surface suggests the course is not Italian, though it plainly is.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter of cured meats and vegetables, served before the pasta, is a course of a meal.

clue.text: The boxer not fancied could be grounded

indicators.note: says the word could be turned into another, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog of the boxer breed, out of favour, might be kept in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests the dog breed, and 'grounded' a dog kept in; 'could be' rearranges GROUNDED.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter not expected to win the bout is the outsider in the betting.

clue.text: Vulgar streak at end of court

parts.note: base means low or vulgar
a line is a streak or stripe

explanation.surface: A coarse stripe of colour or a crude person's habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' is a tennis court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: On a tennis court the boundary at each end, behind which players serve, is this marking.

clue.text: Slow bird with bright body in rudimentary flower

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: a bud is a flower not yet opened
a star is a bright heavenly body

explanation.surface: A slow-moving bird with a vivid form sitting in an unopened bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; STAR goes inside BUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavy ground bird of open plains, which prefers walking to flight, is this species.

clue.text: Promotion for a riser

parts.note: a rise in rank for someone climbing the ladder, playing on a riser as the vertical part of a stair

explanation.surface: Someone who gets up early earns advancement at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A riser is both someone who rises and the upright part of a staircase step, so going higher one stair also describes a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving to a higher position at work is an upward move, like climbing one stair.

clue.text: Developer of jetty unit inside

indicators.note: the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
one is a unit

explanation.surface: A property developer with a single unit on a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developer' suggests property or photographs; it means a trailblazer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who first opens up a new area or technique is a trailblazer who develops it.

clue.text: Eruption to be treated by a house doctor?

definitions.text: to be treated by a house doctor?

explanation.definitionFit: A painful skin rash from the chickenpox virus is one sense; roof tiles of wood, which a roof repairer (a 'doctor' for houses) mends, are the other.

clue.text: The colour for putting on

explanation.definitionFit: The hue of grass is one sense; the short-mown area round a golf hole, where players putt, is the other.

clue.text: Rocket that gets ahead on oxygen

parts.note: read as 'a head': A plus POLL, an old word for the head
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A rocket that takes the lead running on oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' splits into 'a head', A + POLL (poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax); 'on' just places O after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The American space programme that took astronauts to the Moon used Saturn V rockets bearing this name.

clue.text: The first from Leyton Orient is the minutest

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A Leyton Orient player is said to be the smallest in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club; here the two words are split, 'Orient' meaning the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallest or tiniest in amount is the superlative of little.

clue.text: Bookworm pulls up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tows means pulls

explanation.surface: A keen reader tugging something upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOWS round. A swot is British slang for a pupil who studies hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person who reads and learns all the time is a hard-working student.

clue.text: Some fear guesswork and show by reasoning

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used: a run inside them

explanation.surface: Someone fears that guessing may be needed to prove a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run of letters inside 'fear guesswork'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a case through logic, putting forward reasons, is to reason out a position.

clue.text: Towards the pit for the cast

definitions.text: Towards the pit for the cast

parts.words: Towards the pit for the cast
parts.note: the actors on stage moving toward the orchestra pit, at the front of the stage

explanation.surface: Miners heading down to the coal pit, or a mould being cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pit' is the orchestra pit in front of a stage and the 'cast' is the actors, not a mine or a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre direction the front of the stage, near the audience and orchestra, is the lower part, as old stages sloped.

clue.text: Hotel worker on late shift has dark ale

parts.note: night is the dark time of day
porter is a dark British beer

explanation.surface: A hotel employee working nights who enjoys a dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER is a dark British beer brewed with roasted malt; 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff member manning a hotel desk overnight, carrying bags and letting guests in, holds this title.
